detail.body:
## Summary

The gated attention block's two projection GEMMs pin the 256-wide 2-CTA tile (`CONFIG_sm100_128x256x128_128x256x32_cluster2x1_2ctamma`) whenever 256 divides N. That is the right tile for prefill rows and the wrong one at decode row counts: at T = B x S_q <= 128 a projection is a weight-streaming problem, the forced tile pads every M tile to 256 rows, launches one M tile (N / 256 cluster pairs: 52 for the Flash-Next 24/2 fused slab, 10 for its out projection) and runs 3-5x cuBLAS's time. The serving DECODE form pays it twice per step.

This PR adds a **small-M route** to the block's GEMM driver (`kernels/proj_gemm.py`): for a dense bf16 / f16 K-major projection at `m <= 128`, `tile_config="auto"` resolves to a catalog config that already exists -- no new kernel. `swap_ab` puts the **weight rows on the MMA M axis** (every 64- or 128-row weight tile is a CTA, so the machine is filled by N / tile_m CTAs) and the **tokens on the MMA N axis sized to T** (the catalog's N tiles run 8..256 in steps of 8, so an 8-token step issues 64x8 MMAs instead of 256x256 ones); the two-kernel `split_k_slices` fills the machine where the weight has too few rows for one wave. The pick is one-wave arithmetic over the shape and the SM count (`small_m_tile_config`), so a recorded plan name replays. Everything past 128 rows, every fp8 / block-scale / alpha plan and the backward's transposed operands keep today's resolution. The serving DECODE declaration reaches the route through `capture_safe=True` (the JIT-only route; no backend call, no cuDNN handle).

## Measured (Rubin cc 10.7, 212 SMs @ 2376 MHz, one exclusive GPU)

Standalone GEMMs, one process, shuffled A/B/A x 3 rounds x 100 launches, **CUPTI device time** (the split-K arm counts both kernels; the route's plan is the one `tile_config="auto"` builds on this branch), control pair <= 1.1 %, SW-power-cap counter delta 0, speed-up = base / new - 1 (positive = the route is faster). SOL = bytes (weight + activations) against the node's measured HBM copy pin; every weight but the 32/2 slab (143 MB) fits the 126 MB L2 and stays resident across the launches of this micro-benchmark.

**24/2 shard -- fused QKV+gate slab (N 13312, K 2560)**

| 1 | 5.8 | 21.2 | 6.6 | -11.2 % | +223.6 % | 44 % | `64x8 swapAB` |

| T | cuBLAS (us) | FROST forced tile (us) | FROST small-M route (us) | speed-up vs cuBLAS | speed-up vs forced | SOL % (BYTES-HBM) | tile that ran |

| 1 | 4.0 | 11.1 | 4.6 | -13.9 % | +140.3 % | 28 % | `64x8 swapAB` |
| 4 | 8.2 | 10.8 | 4.6 | +77.2 % | +133.1 % | 28 % | `64x8 swapAB` |
| 32 | 4.3 | 10.8 | 4.8 | -11.3 % | +125.3 % | 27 % | `64x32 swapAB` |
| 64 | 4.3 | 10.8 | 5.5 | -21.2 % | +96.8 % | 24 % | `64x64 swapAB` |

The 8/1 shard's two projections stay behind cuBLAS (its weights are 17-38 MB; cuBLAS's own T 4 out-projection pick is the odd one out); the route only closes the gap to the forced tile there -- recorded, not a claim.  Under COLD weights (eight rotating copies, 545 MB > the L2) the route's numbers are unchanged (24/2 slab T 1: 5.9 us) while cuBLAS slows (8.1 -> 9.3), so the comparison above is the conservative one.

**End-to-end serving DECODE step** (the block's paged DECODE form vs vLLM main's own chain -- cuBLAS qkv_proj, the Triton fused norm/RoPE/gate kernel, the paged write, the TensorRT-LLM decode kernel (through FlashInfer), eager sigmoid-mul, cuBLAS o_proj -- both arms in ONE process on identical inputs, CUDA-graph replay, 3 x 100 shuffled, control pair <= 0.9 %, the fp32-oracle check on every arm; 24/2 shard, page 16, KV 4K; each column its own process, the vLLM arm re-measured beside it each time):

| cell | vLLM chain (us) | FROST before (us) | FROST route, stage (1) fused (us) | FROST route, stage (1) unfused (us) | step speed-up vs vLLM: before -> route -> route + unfused | the GEMMs (CUPTI us): before -> route -> route + unfused |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B 1 x KV 4K | 41.8 / 41.9 / 42.5 | 76.9 | 58.6 | **41.3** | -45.6 % -> -28.6 % -> **+2.7 %** | 53.6 (2 x forced) -> 35.6 (fork 27.9 + o_proj 5.5 + reduce 2.2) -> 16.0 (slab 8.2 + o_proj 5.6 + reduce 2.2) + 2.8 norm/RoPE kernel |
| B 32 x KV 4K | 58.2 / 58.4 / 58.5 | 77.3 | 60.8 | **55.2** | -24.7 % -> -4.0 % -> **+5.9 %** | 41.9 -> 25.3 (fork 16.4 + 6.2 + 2.7) -> 17.5 (8.0 + 6.0 + 3.5) + 3.0 norm/RoPE kernel |

"FROST route" = this branch with the serving declaration as it is today (`fuse_norm_rope=True`: stage (1) is the norm + RoPE FORK `proj_gemm_norm_rope.py`, rendered for the 256-wide tile and NOT changed by this PR -- only the out projection takes the route there). "Route + unfused" = the same branch declared `fuse_norm_rope=False` (the plain projection on the route + the block's norm/RoPE kernel): both projections take the route and the step is ahead of vLLM's chain on both cells. The fork at decode row counts (a small-M form of the norm + RoPE epilogue) is the follow-up; the B 1 rows' clock verdict is "no busy sample" (a 41-us step never trips the sampler's 700-W busy threshold; cap counters 0, start clock 2364 MHz), the B 32 rows are CLEAN.

## Tests

- `test_proj_gemm.py`: the rule's names per shape and SM count (RED on the old resolver: the symbol did not exist), the scope gates (fp8 / alpha / block-scale / MN-major keep today's resolution), prefill rows staying on the forced tile, and -- on Rubin -- the plans at T 1 / 4 / 32 / 128 on both 24/2 shapes naming the route's tile, matching `torch.nn.functional.linear` within the module's budget, two launches bitwise equal (the fixed-order reducer).
- `test_block_serving_capture.py`: the flag-free jit-only check now expects the tile `tile_config="auto"` resolves for the plan's own shape (the route at m = 128) instead of the forced name by itself; its intent -- jit-only route, no `frost_gemm` in any ranked list, no cuDNN handle, the kernel runs -- is unchanged.
- An N that 256 does not divide keeps today's resolution (the graph route; under `capture_safe` the typed refusal at the first capture -- the indexer band's + 640 columns are the serving case): the route never names a tile for it; a host cell pins the decline and the refusal.
- The route is an `sm100`-family selection: a process on the `sm120` compiler family (SM 12.x) keeps the graph heuristic's family-aware automatic tile for a small-M projection instead of a catalog name its compiler would refuse (a host cell pins both families).
- The route declines a non-positive extent up front (`n = 0` with a deep K used to divide by a zero CTA count before `build_proj_gemm`'s own extent check could name it; `m = 0` / `k = 0` spelled a tile): `build_proj_gemm` raises its `ValueError` for the extent as it did before the route existed; a host cell pins the four cases.
- `test_proj_gemm.py` / `test_proj_gemm_mxfp8.py`: the two `NormRopeFusionParams` field-order pins name the two fields the paged KV write-through appended after `weight_fp4` (`kv_pool_page_size`, `kv_slot_i64`); both cells had been red on `develop` since that merge (test-only, no library change).
- Development-node tier (Rubin cc 10.7, 204 SMs, shared GPU, functional only), the branch rebased on current `develop`, `-m "L0 or L1"`: `test_proj_gemm.py` 85 passed, `test_proj_gemm_mxfp8.py` 58 passed, `test_block_serving_capture.py` 23 passed, `test_block_serving_decode.py` 99 passed, `test_block_qsa_fp8_kv.py` 20 passed (the e4m3 KV path's projections ride the route too), `test_block_qsa_decode.py` 32 passed (the indexer-band geometry's off-256 contract among them), `test_block_serving_extend.py` 188 passed (its formerly stale L1 cell was fixed upstream in the meantime). Host (A100): the block directory's L0 1138 passed / 0 failed; `gemm/frost/test_gemm_knobs.py` and `test_tile_select_analytic.py` pass among the 525 host cells of the PR's modules and neighbours. At the pre-rebase head: 72 / 99 / 23 / 231 / 116 passed.

## Scope and follow-ups

- Dense bf16 / f16, K-major A and B, no epilogue: the block's forward projections. The route lives in the block's driver, not in the GEMM engine's `select_config` (a scorer change reaches every GEMM caller and needs its own sweep).
- The DECODE form's stage (1) stays on the fused fork at the forced tile under `fuse_norm_rope=True`; the unfused declaration already takes the route on both projections (the table above), and the small-M form of the norm + RoPE epilogue (a per-head reduction across the swapped tile's weight rows) is the follow-up.
- The 8/1 shard's projections remain behind cuBLAS; the route only closes the gap to the forced tile there.

detail.title: frost(gated_attention_block): a small-M tile route for the serving projections at T <= 128 (swap-AB token tiles, split-K on the narrow weight)

files.patch:
@@ -1267,6 +1267,139 @@ def _forced_tile_config(n: int) -> Optional[str]:
     return None
 
 
+# The SMALL-M route: the serving DECODE / MTP projections (T = B x S_q <= SMALL_M_MAX rows).
+#
+# At T <= 128 a projection GEMM is a weight-streaming problem, not an MMA one: the forced 256-wide tile pads every M tile to
+# 256 rows (128 per CTA of the pair), launches ONE M tile (N / 256 cluster pairs: 52 for the 24/2 fused slab, 10 for its
+# out projection) and spends 4-5x cuBLAS's time at T 1..128 (measured on the Rubin perf class, 212 SMs: 25.2 vs 8.4 us at
+# T 1 on the 24/2 fused slab).  The catalog already carries the two axes that fix it, so no new kernel: ``swap_ab``
+# computes ``C^T = W A^T`` with the WEIGHT rows on the MMA M axis (every 64- or 128-row weight tile is a CTA, so the
+# machine is filled by N / tile_m CTAs) and the TOKENS on the MMA N axis, sized to T (the catalog's N tiles run 8..256 in
+# steps of 8, so an 8-token step issues 64x8 / 128x8 MMAs instead of 256x256 ones); the two-kernel ``split_k_slices``
+# fills the machine where the weight has too few rows for one wave (the out projection).  Measured on the Rubin perf
+# class (one process, shuffled A/B/A x 3 x 100, CUPTI device time, control pair <= 0.6 %):
+#
+#   24/2 fused slab (N 13312, K 2560):    T 1   cuBLAS 8.4 | forced 25.3 | 64x8 cluster2x1 swapAB   6.1 us
+#                                         T 4          7.1 |        16.1 | 64x8 cluster2x1 swapAB   6.1
+#                                         T 32         7.2 |        13.5 | 64x32 cluster2x1 swapAB  6.3
+#                                         T 128        9.7 |        13.7 | 128x64 (plain)           9.0
+#   24/2 out projection (N 2560, K 6144): T 1   cuBLAS 7.3 | forced 24.6 | 128x8 splitK8 swapAB    6.3
+#                                         T 4          7.2 |        24.6 | 128x8 splitK8 swapAB    6.4
+#                                         T 32         7.6 |        24.5 | 128x32 splitK8 swapAB   7.0
+#                                         T 128        8.4 |        24.5 | 64x32 (plain)           9.3
+#
+#   32/2 fused slab (N 17408, K 4096):    T 1   cuBLAS 13.3 | forced 45.6 | 128x8 swapAB            13.1
+#                                         T 32        15.8 |        19.9 | 128x32 swapAB           13.3
+#                                         T 128       21+  |        20.3 | 128x128 swapAB          15.5
+#   32/2 out projection (N 4096, K 8192): T 1   cuBLAS 9.5  | forced 32.2 | 128x8 splitK6 swapAB    7.7
+#                                         T 128       14.1 |        32.1 | 128x128 splitK6 swapAB  16.1
+#   8/1 fused slab (N 4608, K 4096):      T 1   cuBLAS 5.8  | forced 21.4 | 64x8 cluster1x1 swapAB  6.6
+#   8/1 out projection (N 4096, K 2048):  T 1   cuBLAS 3.9  | forced 11.2 | 64x8 swapAB (no split)  4.9   (cuBLAS stays ahead on this shard)
+#
+# The rule below spells those picks from the shape and the SM count alone (one-wave arithmetic, no measurement at plan
+# time): the token tile is the power of two >= T; a NARROW weight (fewer than a third of a wave of 64-row tiles) takes
+# 128-row weight tiles with the split-K slice count that fills one wave (capped at 8, every slice at least eight K tiles) up to
+# 64 tokens and the plain 64x32 tile past it while that grid fits one wave -- a shallow K (fewer than 64 K tiles) takes the
+# 64-row swap-AB tile instead of any split; a weight whose 64-row tiles fit one wave takes
+# them (in a 2x1 cluster on a full machine) up to 64 tokens and the plain 128x64 tile past it; a weight whose 64-row tiles
+# overflow a wave takes 128-row weight tiles (one wave).  Dense bf16 / f16, K-major A and B, no epilogue -- the forward's two
+# projections; everything else keeps today's resolution.
+SMALL_M_MAX = 128
+_SMALL_M_SPLIT_K_MAX = 8
+_SMALL_M_CTA_K_ELEMS = 64  # the catalog's 128-byte K tile at 2 bytes per element
+_SMALL_M_SPLIT_K_MIN_K_TILES = 64  # split K only past this depth (K 4096 at 2 bytes): below it the reducer costs more than it buys
+_SMALL_M_MIN_K_TILES_PER_SLICE = 8
+
+
+def small_m_tile_config(
+    m: int,
+    n: int,
+    k: int,
+    *,
+    dtype: torch.dtype,
+    a_major: str = "k",
+    b_major: str = "k",
+    block_scale: bool = False,
+    alpha: bool = False,
+    sm_count: Optional[int] = None,
+) -> Optional[str]:
+    """The catalog config name of the small-M route for a ``[m, k] x [k, n]`` projection, or None when the route does not
+    apply (a non-positive extent, ``m > SMALL_M_MAX``, a dtype other than bf16 / f16, a block-scale or fp8 plan, an MN-major
+    operand, an extent the TMA 16-byte rule refuses, an N that 256 does not divide).  ``sm_count`` is the target's SM count (the active device when None); the SAME shape resolves
+    to the same name on every part of one SM-count class, so a recorded plan name replays."""
+    if m <= 0 or n <= 0 or k <= 0:
+        # a non-positive extent never reaches the one-wave arithmetic below (``n = 0`` would divide by a zero CTA count, ``m`` or
+        # ``k`` at 0 would still spell a tile): the route declines and ``build_proj_gemm``'s own extent check names the extent
+        return None
+    if m > SMALL_M_MAX or block_scale or alpha:
+        return None
+    if dtype not in (torch.bfloat16, torch.float16):
+        return None
+    if a_major != "k" or b_major != "k":
+        return None
+    if n % 8 or k % 8:
+        # The swapped problem reads the weight as the K-contiguous A operand and stores the output M-major: both extents
+        # fall under TMA's 16-byte contiguous-extent rule at 2 bytes per element.
+        return None
+    if n % 256:
+        # An N the forced tile never existed for keeps today's resolution (the graph route; under ``capture_safe`` the typed
+        # refusal at the first capture): the indexer band's + 640 columns (``QsaSpec.index_band``) are the serving case.
+        return None
+    if sm_count is None:
+        from cudnn.gemm.frost.tile_config import _sm_count
+
+        sm_count = _sm_count()
+    tn = 8
+    while tn < m:
+        tn *= 2
+    ctas_64 = -(-n // 64)
+    ctas_128 = -(-n // 128)
+    if 3 * ctas_64 < sm_count:
+        # NARROW weight (fewer than a third of a wave of 64-row tiles).  With a DEEP K (>= 64 K tiles) 128-row weight tiles
+        # and the split-K slice count that fills ONE wave (a slice count that overflows the wave loses its tail: 32/2 out
+        # projection, 32 tiles, S 6 = 192 CTAs 7.7 us vs S 7 = 224 CTAs 9.0 us; every slice at least 8 K tiles); past 64
+        # tokens the plain 64x32 tile where its grid fits one wave, else the same 128x128 split.  With a SHALLOW K the reducer's
+        # fixed cost outweighs the split (8/1 out projection, K 2048: 4.9 us unsplit vs 5.9 split) -- the 64-row swap-AB tile.
+        k_tiles = -(-k // _SMALL_M_CTA_K_ELEMS)
+        slices = (
+            max(1, min(_SMALL_M_SPLIT_K_MAX, sm_count // ctas_128, k_tiles // _SMALL_M_MIN_K_TILES_PER_SLICE)) if k_tiles >= _SMALL_M_SPLIT_K_MIN_K_TILES else 1
+        )
+        if m > 64 and (slices == 1 or -(-m // 64) * -(-n // 32) <= sm_count):
+            return "CONFIG_sm100_64x32x128_64x32x32_cluster1x1_1ctamma"
+        if slices > 1:
+            return f"CONFIG_sm100_128x{tn}x128_128x{tn}x32_cluster1x1_1ctamma_splitK{slices}_swapAB"
+        cluster = "2x1" if 2 * ctas_64 >= sm_count else "1x1"
+        return f"CONFIG_sm100_64x{tn}x128_64x{tn}x32_cluster{cluster}_1ctamma_swapAB"
+    if ctas_64 <= sm_count:
+        # The 64-row weight tile fits one wave.  The 2x1 cluster (the token tile multicast across the pair) pays on a FULL
+        # machine only (24/2 slab, 208 CTAs: +18 %; 8/1 slab, 72 CTAs: -10 %).
+        if m <= 64:
+            cluster = "2x1" if 2 * ctas_64 >= sm_count else "1x1"
+            return f"CONFIG_sm100_64x{tn}x128_64x{tn}x32_cluster{cluster}_1ctamma_swapAB"
+        # 65..128 tokens: the plain 128-token x 64-weight tile (full-rate MMA M) while its grid fits one wave.
+        if -(-m // 128) * ctas_64 <= sm_count:
+            return "CONFIG_sm100_128x64x128_128x64x32_cluster1x1_1ctamma"
+        return "CONFIG_sm100_128x128x128_128x128x32_cluster1x1_1ctamma_swapAB"
+    # The 64-row tiles overflow a wave: 128-row weight tiles (one wave up to N = 128 x SMs; 32/2 slab, 136 CTAs).
+    if m <= 64:
+        return f"CONFIG_sm100_128x{tn}x128_128x{tn}x32_cluster1x1_1ctamma_swapAB"
+    return "CONFIG_sm100_128x128x128_128x128x32_cluster1x1_1ctamma_swapAB"
+
+
+def _auto_tile_name(m: int, n: int, k: int, *, dtype: torch.dtype, a_major: str, b_major: str, block_scale: bool, alpha: bool) -> Optional[str]:
+    """``tile_config="auto"``: the small-M route where it applies (:func:`small_m_tile_config`; on the ``sm100`` compiler family
+    only -- its names are the tcgen05 tree's catalog, so a process on the ``sm120`` family keeps the family-aware fallback below),
+    else the forced 256-wide tile where 256 divides N (:func:`_forced_tile_config`), else None (the graph heuristic's own tile)."""
+    from cudnn.gemm.frost import arch_family
+
+    name = (
+        small_m_tile_config(m, n, k, dtype=dtype, a_major=a_major, b_major=b_major, block_scale=block_scale, alpha=alpha)
+        if arch_family.active_family() == "sm100"
+        else None
+    )
+    return name if name is not None else _forced_tile_config(n)
+
+
 def build_proj_gemm(
     *,
     m: int,
@@ -1469,9 +1602,12 @@ def build_proj_gemm(
             f"{label}: capture_safe=True needs the forced-tile JIT route, and pin_frost=False is the graph route by request (its first execute "
             "per stream creates a cuDNN handle, which cannot happen inside a CUDA-graph capture); drop one of the two"
         )

+        (128, _FLASH_NEXT_24_2["d_model"], _FLASH_NEXT_24_2["k_o"], "CONFIG_sm100_64x32x128_64x32x32_cluster1x1_1ctamma"),
+        # the 32/2 shard: 272 64-row tiles overflow a wave -> 128-row weight tiles (136 CTAs), no split; its out projection
+        # (32 tiles of 128 rows over K 8192) splits 6 ways = one wave; past 64 tokens 2 x 128 plain tiles overflow -> the split
+        (1, (2 * 32 + 2 * 2) * 256, 4096, "CONFIG_sm100_128x8x128_128x8x32_cluster1x1_1ctamma_swapAB"),
+        (128, (2 * 32 + 2 * 2) * 256, 4096, "CONFIG_sm100_128x128x128_128x128x32_cluster1x1_1ctamma_swapAB"),
+        (1, 4096, 32 * 256, "CONFIG_sm100_128x8x128_128x8x32_cluster1x1_1ctamma_splitK6_swapAB"),
+        (128, 4096, 32 * 256, "CONFIG_sm100_128x128x128_128x128x32_cluster1x1_1ctamma_splitK6_swapAB"),
+        # the 8/1 shard's slab: 72 64-row tiles (a third of the machine) -> the 64-row tile without the pair's multicast
+        (1, (2 * 8 + 2 * 1) * 256, 4096, "CONFIG_sm100_64x8x128_64x8x32_cluster1x1_1ctamma_swapAB"),
+        # its out projection is narrow but SHALLOW (K 2048 = 32 K tiles): no split pays -> the 64-row swap-AB tile, the plain

+        (1, 4096, 8 * 256, "CONFIG_sm100_64x8x128_64x8x32_cluster1x1_1ctamma_swapAB"),
+        (128, 4096, 8 * 256, "CONFIG_sm100_64x32x128_64x32x32_cluster1x1_1ctamma"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_small_m_route_names_a_swap_ab_tile_for_decode_row_counts(m, n, k, expect):
+    """The route is a pure function of the shape and the SM count: the token tile is the power of two >= T, the weight
+    tile and the slice count follow the weight's width.  Every name it spells resolves in the catalog grammar."""
+    from cudnn.gemm.frost.tile_config import by_name
+
+    name = small_m_tile_config(m, n, k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, sm_count=_RUBIN_SMS)
+    assert name == expect
+    cfg = by_name(name)
+    assert cfg.swap_ab == name.endswith("_swapAB")
+    assert cfg.cta_tile_n >= min(m, 128) or not cfg.swap_ab  # the token tile covers the step
+
+
+def test_small_m_route_leaves_prefill_rows_on_the_forced_tile():
+    """Past SMALL_M_MAX nothing changes: the 256-wide forced tile is the prefill / training plan it always was."""
+    n, k = _FLASH_NEXT_24_2["n_qkvg"], _FLASH_NEXT_24_2["d_model"]
+    assert small_m_tile_config(SMALL_M_MAX + 1, n, k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, sm_count=_RUBIN_SMS) is None
+    assert small_m_tile_config(8192, n, k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, sm_count=_RUBIN_SMS) is None
+    from cudnn.gated_attention_block.kernels.proj_gemm import _auto_tile_name
+
+    assert _auto_tile_name(8192, n, k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, a_major="k", b_major="k", block_scale=False, alpha=False) == _FORCED_TILE_NAME
+    assert _auto_tile_name(1, n, k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, a_major="k", b_major="k", block_scale=False, alpha=False) != _FORCED_TILE_NAME
